references.label: HMI dry-grain tAs pooled reference
references.methods: HMI calculates a pooled distribution of subgroup medians across the admitted sampling families. Each family has equal total weight, then each country, township or rice category within that family has equal weight. This estimates the position of a typical source subgroup, not the median of every individual rice sample worldwide. Raw measurements first supply subgroup medians; published subgroup medians remain summary units. Study means, maxima and ranges are never inserted as individual samples. The rating evaluates the row’s displayed source mean or median against the pooled subgroup-median distribution; a mean is not relabelled as a median, and skewed distributions can give different positions for these statistics. The same frozen reference is used for every eligible finding and does not change with filters. FDA rice categories and Myanmar townships share an explicitly dry-weight grain basis. They are pooled to describe central concentrations across ordinary market and farm evidence, with equal family weights. Hao’s mining-area mean is evaluated against this reference but does not set it; conversion to dry mass is bounded by the reported 0–13% residual moisture.
references.limitations: The collection is historical and geographically uneven, with small numbers of sampling families. Country, township and category subgroups have different sampling frames. It is an evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world market. Source analytical and rounding uncertainty remains; censoring bounds are not confidence intervals. The selected finding can contribute to its reference. Low / Moderate / High describes concentration position, not health risk, compliance, certainty or a causal rice-form effect. FDA trace estimates retain analytical uncertainty; non-speciated species are bounded by total arsenic.

references.label: HMI dry-grain iAs pooled reference
references.methods: HMI calculates a pooled distribution of subgroup medians across the admitted sampling families. Each family has equal total weight, then each country, township or rice category within that family has equal weight. This estimates the position of a typical source subgroup, not the median of every individual rice sample worldwide. Raw measurements first supply subgroup medians; published subgroup medians remain summary units. Study means, maxima and ranges are never inserted as individual samples. The rating evaluates the row’s displayed source mean or median against the pooled subgroup-median distribution; a mean is not relabelled as a median, and skewed distributions can give different positions for these statistics. The same frozen reference is used for every eligible finding and does not change with filters. FDA category medians are calculated from its full analytical rice table; Carey’s regional medians supply a separate family. Dry-weight and freeze-dried grain are admitted on dry mass, retaining preparation differences. The Carey atmospheric column is excluded. Hao’s mining-area mean is an external target with a bounded 0–13% residual-moisture conversion; it does not set the reference.
references.limitations: The collection is historical and geographically uneven, with small numbers of sampling families. Country, township and category subgroups have different sampling frames. It is an evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world market. Source analytical and rounding uncertainty remains; censoring bounds are not confidence intervals. The selected finding can contribute to its reference. Low / Moderate / High describes concentration position, not health risk, compliance, certainty or a causal rice-form effect. Published subgroup counts do not sum to article totals (Carey 1,093 versus 1,180; Shi 2,277 versus 2,270). Counts are not used for primary weights; the count-weighted sensitivity inherits this discrepancy. FDA trace estimates retain analytical uncertainty; non-speciated species are bounded by total arsenic.

references.label: HMI dry-grain DMA pooled reference
references.methods: HMI calculates a pooled distribution of subgroup medians across the admitted sampling families. Each family has equal total weight, then each country, township or rice category within that family has equal weight. This estimates the position of a typical source subgroup, not the median of every individual rice sample worldwide. Raw measurements first supply subgroup medians; published subgroup medians remain summary units. Study means, maxima and ranges are never inserted as individual samples. The rating evaluates the row’s displayed source mean or median against the pooled subgroup-median distribution; a mean is not relabelled as a median, and skewed distributions can give different positions for these statistics. The same frozen reference is used for every eligible finding and does not change with filters. FDA category medians and Carey regional medians are pooled as two families on a dry-grain basis. Total and inorganic arsenic are excluded from this DMA reference. Carey medians at or below 3 are bounded 0–3 because the abstract and methods differ on the reporting limit.
references.limitations: The collection is historical and geographically uneven, with small numbers of sampling families. Country, township and category subgroups have different sampling frames. It is an evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world market. Source analytical and rounding uncertainty remains; censoring bounds are not confidence intervals. The selected finding can contribute to its reference. Low / Moderate / High describes concentration position, not health risk, compliance, certainty or a causal rice-form effect. Published subgroup counts do not sum to article totals (Carey 1,093 versus 1,180; Shi 2,277 versus 2,270). Counts are not used for primary weights; the count-weighted sensitivity inherits this discrepancy. FDA trace estimates retain analytical uncertainty; non-speciated species are bounded by total arsenic.

references.label: HMI dry-grain Cd pooled reference
references.methods: HMI calculates a pooled distribution of subgroup medians across the admitted sampling families. Each family has equal total weight, then each country, township or rice category within that family has equal weight. This estimates the position of a typical source subgroup, not the median of every individual rice sample worldwide. Raw measurements first supply subgroup medians; published subgroup medians remain summary units. Study means, maxima and ranges are never inserted as individual samples. The rating evaluates the row’s displayed source mean or median against the pooled subgroup-median distribution; a mean is not relabelled as a median, and skewed distributions can give different positions for these statistics. The same frozen reference is used for every eligible finding and does not change with filters. Myanmar township medians and Shi country medians share dry-grain concentration units. Shi’s compilation is one family; its component publications are not added again. Half-LOD country medians are bounded 0–9.8 µg/kg. The inconsistent Mauritius Q1 is not used. Hao’s targeted mining-area mean is a comparison target, not a reference member.
references.limitations: The collection is historical and geographically uneven, with small numbers of sampling families. Country, township and category subgroups have different sampling frames. It is an evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world market. Source analytical and rounding uncertainty remains; censoring bounds are not confidence intervals. The selected finding can contribute to its reference. Low / Moderate / High describes concentration position, not health risk, compliance, certainty or a causal rice-form effect. Published subgroup counts do not sum to article totals (Carey 1,093 versus 1,180; Shi 2,277 versus 2,270). Counts are not used for primary weights; the count-weighted sensitivity inherits this discrepancy.

references.label: HMI uncooked-grain tAs pooled reference
references.methods: HMI calculates a pooled distribution of subgroup medians across the admitted sampling families. Each family has equal total weight, then each country, township or rice category within that family has equal weight. This estimates the position of a typical source subgroup, not the median of every individual rice sample worldwide. Raw measurements first supply subgroup medians; published subgroup medians remain summary units. Study means, maxima and ranges are never inserted as individual samples. The rating evaluates the row’s displayed source mean or median against the pooled subgroup-median distribution; a mean is not relabelled as a median, and skewed distributions can give different positions for these statistics. The same frozen reference is used for every eligible finding and does not change with filters. Myanmar dry-weight observations are converted to original grain mass with the study’s measured 6–7% moisture loss (×0.93–0.94); Saudi ground-grain measurements retain their analysed mass. No generic moisture assumption is applied. These ordinary farm/market sampling frames form a historical international occurrence reference. Saudi subgroups retain reported origin; triplicate laboratory analyses count once per rice sample. Song’s fresh-weight mean and Tran’s air-dried genotype estimates are external comparisons at native grain moisture; they do not set the reference. Residual moisture and experimental field selection limit those comparisons. Yan’s censored median is 0–LOD, not its published half-LOD point.
references.limitations: The collection is historical and geographically uneven, with small numbers of sampling families. Country, township and category subgroups have different sampling frames. It is an evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world market. Source analytical and rounding uncertainty remains; censoring bounds are not confidence intervals. The selected finding can contribute to its reference. Low / Moderate / High describes concentration position, not health risk, compliance, certainty or a causal rice-form effect.
